item.title: Note: UART monitor - observing transmission over UART
item.description: Connecting MSP430 to SIM900 When using UART, for debugging purposes, I needed to monitor what the MSP430 sends and what the second device (SIM900) responds. To do this, you need to remove the MCU from the LaunchPad and connect it independently (for example, on a breadboard). And connect the LaunchPad itself to the computer to monitor the UART. item.title: MSP430 Interfacing to SIM900A
item.description: For pitfalls of the SIM900A Mini v3.4 board read here. UART wiring scheme is simple: RX to TX, TX to RX. Power supply for SIM900A: for bootup 3.3V from the LaunchPad was sufficient for me, though it violates the datasheet (4V required). Nevertheless, everything works. Initially jumpers are in this position for UART conversion through MAX232: But we don’t need to connect the board to a computer COM port, we need the unconverted UART signal.

item.title: Don't buy SIM900A! SIM900A Mini v3.4 board
item.description: Connecting MSP430 to SIM900A UART monitor - observing data transmission over UART I ordered a soldered SIM900A on the SIM900A Mini v3.4 board, without fully understanding how the SIM900A modification differs from the SIM900. The main difference is that SIM900A operates in a dual-band range, while SIM900 operates in quad-band. It seemed that for Ukraine, dual-band should fit ideally. But no. SIM900A has a regional lock.
